title: Building Age and Vacancy Permit Pricing on the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy
content:
An empty older building deteriorates faster, and the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy prices a vacancy permit on such a building with building-age points added to the permit rate percentage.

**Rule.** The building's age is counted in whole months from January 1 of the year built to the request date. A building more than 100 years old on the request date (more than 1200 whole months) adds 10 points; one more than 70 but not more than 100 years old (more than 840 and up to 1200 whole months) adds 5 points; a building 70 years old or younger (840 whole months or fewer) adds no points.

The points are percentage points added into the permit rate percentage of the permit being requested, before that rate is applied, once, in the charge.

## Bands

| Whole months from January 1 of the year built to the request date | Age reading | Building-age points |
|---|---|---|
| more than 1200 | more than 100 years | 10 |
| 841 to 1200 | more than 70, not more than 100 years | 5 |
| 840 or fewer | 70 years or younger | 0 |

## Both sides of each threshold (hypothetical dates)

| Year built | Request date | Whole months | Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1925 | 20 January 2025 | 1200 | 5 |
| 1925 | 1 February 2025 | 1201 | 10 |
| 1955 | 15 January 2025 | 840 | 0 |
| 1955 | 1 February 2025 | 841 | 5 |

The count starts on January 1 of the year built whatever the month of construction, and only completed months count: 1200 months and 19 days is still 1200 whole months.
